fields.summary: The prior art (DME) accomplishes playback of selected media in synchrony on a selected set of playback devices when a scene is invoked, but does not allow for continuous output of media on a particular playback device and joining of that continuous output by a selected playback device or set thereof in synchrony with media currently playing back on the particular playback device, i.e., the prior art only teaches synchronization as the start of the process, whereas the claims require invocation of a scene that adds a playback device or group to join a currently-playing device without pause/interruption or user re-engagement with playback controls.

items.quote: the prior art does not reasonably teach the subject matter of the independent claims. Particularly while DME operates to accomplish playback of selected media in synchrony on a selected set of first, second, etc. playback devices when a scene is invoked upon said set of players, DME does not allow for continuous output of media on a particular playback device and joining of the continuous output by a selected playback device or set thereof in synchrony with media currently playing back upon the particular playback device.

fields.summary: An examiner's amendment was entered, authorized by Brandon Kennedy in an interview on 8/30/19, amending independent claims 1, 9, and 17 and dependent claims 2, 5, 10, 13, and 18. The amendments primarily replace the phrase "play back" with "output" in various limitations describing synchronous media output between zone players (e.g., causing a zone player to coordinate with another zone player to output media in synchrony rather than "play back" media in synchrony), across claims reciting creation, storage, and invocation of first and second zone scenes and transitions between standalone and grouped playback modes.
